newsitem.title: UK: Oil stocks seen sharply up over rest of 97 - IEA.
newsitem.headline: Oil stocks seen sharply up over rest of 97 - IEA.

text.p: Projections of world oil demand and non-OPEC supply for the remainder of the year suggest that there will be very substantial rises in oil stocks, unless OPEC crude oil output falls significantly, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Tuesday.
In a section of its Monthly Oil Market Report titled "Where will additional stockbuilds go?" the IEA said there could be a major build up of oil stocks during the rest of the year.
Despite world oil supply outstripping demand over the past three months a big stock build that many observers expected failed to take place, the IEA said.
It appears to have been put off to the second half of the year when aggregate inventories could well rise above 1996 levels.
Most significantly the lack of a stockdraw in 1Q97 and the build in 2Q97 have resulted in an estimated increase of 74 million barrels in total OECD stocks versus June 1996.
This offset much of the 81 million barrel fall between June 1995 and June 1996.

With OECD stocks now back nearly to pre-1996 levels and the motivation for "just-in-time" stock practices by many major oil companies to enhance reported short-term financial performance it is unclear where the implied second half 1997 stockbuilds would occur.
The most likely rise may be in non-OECD stocks, particularly those in producer controlled storage and oil in transit due to "slow steaming" and a rising number of distressed cargoes, the IEA said.
